source: Workout App v1.5 — Recovery & Stretching (Future Updates), Part 2 research, 2026-11-17

safety.disclaimer: These exercises are general information, not medical advice. They are not a diagnosis or a treatment plan. If you have had surgery, a recent injury, numbness, weakness, or pain that is getting worse, see a doctor or physiotherapist before starting. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain.

painRule.text: 0–3 out of 10 during an exercise is OK.
4–5 out of 10 is acceptable only if it settles by the next morning.
6+ out of 10, or pain that is worse the next day: stop that exercise and drop back a step.

safety.phasing: Each list runs early → late. Level 3 moves are only for when Level 1–2 feel comfortable.
safety.shoulderPrompt: Can you raise your arm above shoulder height without sharp pain?
safety.shoulderRule: MOON shoulder protocol: don't start strengthening until the arm lifts above about 120° and pain at rest is below 2/10. Until then, the mobility moves only.
safety.ankleRule: After a fresh sprain, do NOT tilt the foot in or out for the first ~2 weeks — only bend and straighten (pumps). No running or jumping until your balance is back.
safety.equipment: Everything here is bodyweight plus one loop resistance band. The band is the only purchase; it fits in a glove box.
safety.stretchRule: Move to warm up, hold to cool down: keep pre-workout stretches moving, and save long holds for after the workout (Cleveland Clinic / Harvard Health).

areas.name: Knees
areas.intro: achy knees from sitting, stairs, and squatting loads; patellofemoral pain ("runner's knee") and early osteoarthritis are the usual culprits. The evidence base is consistent: strengthen quads + glutes/hips, don't just stretch the knee (Lack et al., *BJSM* 2015: hip + quad strengthening cut patellofemoral pain 50–75%).

exercises.name: Quad sets (isometric)
exercises.how: Leg straight, tighten thigh, press back of knee into floor/bed, hold 5–10 s. First exercise prescribed after knee replacement — safe for almost everyone.
steps: Leg straight, tighten thigh, press back of knee into floor/bed, hold 5–10 s.
First exercise prescribed after knee replacement — safe for almost everyone.

exercises.name: Straight-leg raises
exercises.how: Lying on back, one knee bent, lift straight leg 6–10 in, hold 5 s, lower slowly.
steps: Lying on back, one knee bent, lift straight leg 6–10 in, hold 5 s, lower slowly.

exercises.name: Heel slides
exercises.how: Lying down, slide heel toward buttocks to bend the knee as far as comfortable, hold 2 s. Restores range of motion.
steps: Lying down, slide heel toward buttocks to bend the knee as far as comfortable, hold 2 s.
Restores range of motion.

exercises.name: Seated knee extensions (short-arc quads)
exercises.how: Sitting, tighten thigh and slowly straighten the leg, hold 5 s. Isolates the VMO (inner quad, key for kneecap tracking).
steps: Sitting, tighten thigh and slowly straighten the leg, hold 5 s.
Isolates the VMO (inner quad, key for kneecap tracking).

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.how: Lying on back, knees bent, squeeze glutes and lift hips to a straight line shoulders–knees.
steps: Lying on back, knees bent, squeeze glutes and lift hips to a straight line shoulders–knees.

exercises.name: Clamshell
exercises.how: Side-lying, knees bent, feet together, open top knee without rolling hips back. Targets gluteus medius (hip stability → less knee load).
steps: Side-lying, knees bent, feet together, open top knee without rolling hips back.
Targets gluteus medius (hip stability → less knee load).

exercises.name: Wall sit (shallow)
exercises.how: Back against wall, slide down only a little, hold 10–20 s. Build depth slowly.
steps: Back against wall, slide down only a little, hold 10–20 s.
Build depth slowly.
exercises.gifNote: Demo shows a deeper wall sit; keep yours shallow

exercises.name: Mini squats / half squats
exercises.how: Feet shoulder-width, lower hips ~10 in as if sitting into a chair, hold 5 s, push up through heels.
steps: Feet shoulder-width, lower hips ~10 in as if sitting into a chair, hold 5 s, push up through heels.

exercises.name: Step-ups
exercises.how: Low step (truck step works), step up leading with the sore leg, 2×10 each leg. Progress height slowly.
steps: Low step (truck step works), step up leading with the sore leg, 2×10 each leg.
Progress height slowly.

exercises.name: Standing hamstring curls
exercises.how: Holding a chair/wall, bend knee and raise heel toward ceiling, hold 5 s.
steps: Holding a chair/wall, bend knee and raise heel toward ceiling, hold 5 s.

exercises.name: Calf raises
exercises.how: Holding a chair, rise onto toes as high as possible, lower slowly. 2×10.
steps: Holding a chair, rise onto toes as high as possible, lower slowly.

exercises.name: Hamstring towel stretch
exercises.how: Lying or sitting, loop towel around foot, gently pull leg toward you until a mild stretch, hold 30 s.
steps: Lying or sitting, loop towel around foot, gently pull leg toward you until a mild stretch, hold 30 s.

areas.swapsText: jump squats → mini squats · lunges → step-ups · running/jump rope → walking or cycling · burpees → incline push-up + step-back (no jump) · deep squats → wall sit or sit-to-stand.

swaps.match: deep squat|pistol|one leg squat|1 legged|prison squat|squat

areas.cautions: avoid deep squats, lunges with the knee travelling well past the toes, and jumping during a flare-up (https://www.physioipoh.com.my/blog/best-exercises-knee-pain/). Wall sits: keep the bend shallow — a full 90° wall sit loads the knee heavily and some sources advise against it for knee problems. Stop and see a clinician for a swollen, locked, or giving-way knee, or pain that doesn't settle within 6–8 weeks.
redFlags: A swollen, locked, or giving-way knee.
Pain that doesn't settle within 6–8 weeks.
areas.laterCandidates: standing quad stretch, single-leg stand (balance), step-downs (eccentric, later phase), lateral band walks, side-lying hip abduction/adduction.

areas.name: Ankles/feet
areas.intro: sprains (often old, never properly rehabbed — up to 40% of people have lingering pain/instability after a lateral sprain; chronic instability rates up to 70% in some studies). Rehab is phased: mobility → isometric strength → banded strength → balance.

exercises.name: Ankle alphabet
exercises.how: Seated, trace A–Z in the air with the big toe. Restores range of motion in all directions.
steps: Seated, trace A–Z in the air with the big toe.
Restores range of motion in all directions.
exercises.caution: After a fresh sprain (first ~2 weeks) keep to up-and-down movement only; skip the side-to-side part.

exercises.name: Ankle circles / rotations
exercises.how: Slow circles each way, 5–10 reps. Reduces stiffness and swelling.
steps: Slow circles each way, 5–10 reps.
Reduces stiffness and swelling.
exercises.caution: After a fresh sprain (first ~2 weeks) keep to up-and-down movement only; skip the side-to-side part.

exercises.name: Ankle pumps (dorsiflexion / plantarflexion)
exercises.how: Point toes away, then pull toes up toward shin, slow and controlled.
steps: Point toes away, then pull toes up toward shin, slow and controlled.

exercises.name: Towel scrunches / toe pick-ups
exercises.how: Spread a towel on the floor, scrunch it toward you with your toes; or pick up small objects with toes. Builds foot/ankle strength.
steps: Spread a towel on the floor, scrunch it toward you with your toes; or pick up small objects with toes.
Builds foot/ankle strength.

exercises.name: Seated heel raises
exercises.how: Sitting, feet flat, push through toes to lift heels, lower slowly. 10–15 reps.
steps: Sitting, feet flat, push through toes to lift heels, lower slowly.
10–15 reps.

exercises.name: Isometric eversion
exercises.how: Seated, outside of foot pressed against a wall/furniture, push outward without moving, hold 6 s. Strengthens the peroneals (the muscles that stop the ankle rolling).
steps: Seated, outside of foot pressed against a wall/furniture, push outward without moving, hold 6 s.
Strengthens the peroneals (the muscles that stop the ankle rolling).

exercises.name: Isometric inversion / opposition
exercises.how: Press inside of foot against the other foot, hold 6 s; then press down against the other heel.
steps: Press inside of foot against the other foot, hold 6 s; then press down against the other heel.

exercises.name: Banded eversion
exercises.how: Loop band around ball of foot, anchor other end, rotate ankle outward against resistance, return slowly. 2×15.
steps: Loop band around ball of foot, anchor other end, rotate ankle outward against resistance, return slowly.

exercises.name: Banded inversion
exercises.how: Same setup, rotate ankle inward against the band.
steps: Same setup, rotate ankle inward against the band.

exercises.name: Banded dorsiflexion
exercises.how: Band around foot, pull toes up toward shin against resistance.
steps: Band around foot, pull toes up toward shin against resistance.

exercises.name: Standing heel raises (supported)
exercises.how: Holding a wall/rail, rise onto toes, hold 5 s, lower slowly. 10–15 reps. Progress to single leg.
steps: Holding a wall/rail, rise onto toes, hold 5 s, lower slowly.
10–15 reps.
Progress to single leg.

exercises.name: Single-leg balance
exercises.how: Stand next to support, lift one foot, balance as long as possible; aim for 60 s × 3 on the injured leg. The key re-injury prevention exercise.
steps: Stand next to support, lift one foot, balance as long as possible; aim for 60 s × 3 on the injured leg.
The key re-injury prevention exercise.

areas.swapsText: jump rope / running → walking, cycling, or seated cardio · jumping jacks → step jacks · lunges → supported step-ups · calf-heavy work → seated heel raises.
areas.cautions: after a fresh sprain, do NOT tilt the foot in/out for the first ~2 weeks — only bend/straighten — as that can re-injure ligaments (https://www.orthoanswer.org/foot-and-ankle/rehabilitation-for-ankle-sprain/). No running or jumping until balance is restored. Grade 2 (partial tear, can't walk comfortably) and Grade 3 (complete tear, unstable) sprains need medical assessment before loading — the app should say so. If problems persist 6–8 weeks after injury, see a physiotherapist.
redFlags: You can't put weight on the foot or can't walk comfortably (possible grade 2–3 sprain): get it assessed before loading it.
The ankle feels unstable, or problems last 6–8 weeks after the injury.
areas.laterCandidates: toe raises against a wall, star balance (reach foot to points around you), heel-toe walking, bent-knee calf stretch, wobble-board work (needs a board — not truck-friendly, skip for v1.5).

areas.name: Hips
areas.intro: stiff/achy hips from 10+ hours sitting, weak glutes (gluteus medius especially — it keeps the pelvis level with every step). Hip pain also drives knee and back pain, so this area overlaps both.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.how: As knee #5. Cornerstone hip exercise: strengthens glutes, stretches tight hip flexors, no spinal load.
steps: As knee #5.
Cornerstone hip exercise: strengthens glutes, stretches tight hip flexors, no spinal load.

exercises.name: Clamshell
exercises.how: As knee #6. Isolates gluteus medius, the key pelvic stabiliser.
steps: As knee #6.
Isolates gluteus medius, the key pelvic stabiliser.

exercises.name: Side-lying leg raise
exercises.how: Lying on side, bottom knee bent, top leg straight, lift to ~45°, lower slowly. Outer hip / glute med.
steps: Lying on side, bottom knee bent, top leg straight, lift to ~45°, lower slowly.
Outer hip / glute med.

exercises.name: Standing hip abduction
exercises.how: Standing, holding support, lift leg out to the side without leaning.
steps: Standing, holding support, lift leg out to the side without leaning.

exercises.name: Sit-to-stand
exercises.how: From a sturdy chair, lean forward slightly and stand without pushing with arms; sit back slowly. Retrains hip drive.
steps: From a sturdy chair, lean forward slightly and stand without pushing with arms; sit back slowly.
Retrains hip drive.

exercises.name: Single-leg bridge
exercises.how: Glute bridge on one leg, other leg lifted. Strength + balance; progress from #1.
steps: Glute bridge on one leg, other leg lifted.
Strength + balance; progress from #1.

exercises.name: Banded side steps / monster walk
exercises.how: Loop band above knees, slight knee bend, 10 small steps sideways and back. Needs a loop band (small, truck-friendly).
steps: Loop band above knees, slight knee bend, 10 small steps sideways and back.
Needs a loop band (small, truck-friendly).

exercises.name: Hip hikers
exercises.how: Standing on a low step on one leg, let the other hip drop then lift it level. Pure glute-med work.
steps: Standing on a low step on one leg, let the other hip drop then lift it level.
Pure glute-med work.

exercises.name: Straight-leg raises (side-lying)
exercises.how: Lying on side or back, lift straight leg to strengthen hip flexors/abductors without joint stress.
steps: Lying on side or back, lift straight leg to strengthen hip flexors/abductors without joint stress.

exercises.name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
exercises.how: Kneeling lunge, back knee down, push hips forward, hold 30 s. The #1 stretch for sitters.
steps: Kneeling lunge, back knee down, push hips forward, hold 30 s.
The #1 stretch for sitters.

exercises.name: Figure-four stretch
exercises.how: Lying or seated, ankle on opposite knee, lean forward gently. Stretches piriformis/glutes.
steps: Lying or seated, ankle on opposite knee, lean forward gently.
Stretches piriformis/glutes.
exercises.gifNote: Lying version shown (seated is fine too)

exercises.name: Bird dog
exercises.how: On all fours, extend opposite arm + leg, keep spine and hips still, hold 5–10 s. Core + hip + pelvis coordination.
steps: On all fours, extend opposite arm + leg, keep spine and hips still, hold 5–10 s.
Core + hip + pelvis coordination.

areas.swapsText: deep squats → sit-to-stand or shallow squats · lunges → step-ups · high knees → marching in place · running → walking.
areas.cautions: sharp or catching pain in the joint = stop (mild muscle fatigue is expected; joint catching is not). After hip surgery, surgeon/therapist precautions override everything in the app. Mild discomfort during exercise is acceptable only if it has settled by the next day.
redFlags: Sharp or catching pain in the joint (mild muscle tiredness is normal; joint catching is not).
After hip surgery, your surgeon's or therapist's precautions override everything in the app.
areas.laterCandidates: 90/90 hip stretch, pigeon pose, hip circles, prone hip extension, clock toe taps (balance).

areas.name: Lower back
areas.intro: the big one for truckers — long sitting, then lifting. The evidence-based core is spine-sparing core endurance, not sit-ups: Prof. Stuart McGill's "Big 3" (curl-up, side plank, bird dog) is the most widely used physio starting point. General rule: exercise is first-line treatment for non-specific low back pain; staying gently active beats rest.

exercises.name: McGill curl-up
exercises.how: Lying on back, one knee bent, hands under low back, lift head/shoulders just until shoulder blades clear, hold 10 s. Trains front core WITHOUT bending the spine.
steps: Lying on back, one knee bent, hands under low back, lift head/shoulders just until shoulder blades clear, hold 10 s.
Trains front core WITHOUT bending the spine.
exercises.source: https://befittrainingphysio.com/blog/low-back-pain-try-the-mcgill-big-3/ ; video of McGill himself: https://pro-activehealth.com/back-health/ (embeds YouTube video ID MaZbI2Tp2-g)

exercises.name: Side plank (from knees)
exercises.how: On side, elbow under shoulder, knees bent, lift hips to a straight line head–knees, hold 10 s. Progress to straight legs.
steps: On side, elbow under shoulder, knees bent, lift hips to a straight line head–knees, hold 10 s.
Progress to straight legs.

exercises.name: Bird dog
exercises.how: As hip #12. The back-extensor leg of the Big 3.
steps: As hip #12.
The back-extensor leg of the Big 3.

exercises.name: Dead bug
exercises.how: Lying on back, arms up, knees at 90°, flatten low back into floor, slowly extend opposite arm + leg. Teaches the core to hold the spine still while limbs move.
steps: Lying on back, arms up, knees at 90°, flatten low back into floor, slowly extend opposite arm + leg.
Teaches the core to hold the spine still while limbs move.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.how: As knee #5. Glutes support the back; weak glutes = overloaded spine.
steps: As knee #5.
Glutes support the back; weak glutes = overloaded spine.

exercises.name: Cat-cow
exercises.how: On all fours, slowly arch then round the spine, 8–10 slow rounds. Gentle spinal mobility, good first thing.
steps: On all fours, slowly arch then round the spine, 8–10 slow rounds.
Gentle spinal mobility, good first thing.

exercises.name: Knee-to-chest stretch
exercises.how: Lying on back, pull one knee to chest, hold 30 s. Gentle low-back release.
steps: Lying on back, pull one knee to chest, hold 30 s.
Gentle low-back release.
exercises.source: Standard physio; see stretching sources below

exercises.name: Child's pose
exercises.how: Kneeling, sit back toward heels, arms extended forward, hold 30 s.
steps: Kneeling, sit back toward heels, arms extended forward, hold 30 s.

exercises.name: Pelvic tilts
exercises.how: Lying on back, knees bent, gently flatten low back into the floor by tilting pelvis, hold 5 s. Wakes up deep core.
steps: Lying on back, knees bent, gently flatten low back into the floor by tilting pelvis, hold 5 s.
Wakes up deep core.

exercises.name: Cobra / press-up (gentle)
exercises.how: Lying face down, press chest up on forearms/hands, hips stay down, hold briefly. Only if it feels good.
steps: Lying face down, press chest up on forearms/hands, hips stay down, hold briefly.
Only if it feels good.

exercises.name: Supine twist (gentle)
exercises.how: Lying on back, knees bent, slowly let knees fall to one side, hold 30 s. Keep shoulders down.
steps: Lying on back, knees bent, slowly let knees fall to one side, hold 30 s.
Keep shoulders down.
exercises.source: Standard physio; see stretching sources below

exercises.name: Sit-to-stand
exercises.how: As hip #5. Leg strength without spinal load — the functional move that protects the back in daily life.
steps: As hip #5.
Leg strength without spinal load — the functional move that protects the back in daily life.

areas.swapsText: sit-ups / crunches → McGill curl-up or dead bug · toe-touch stretches → hip hinge or hamstring stretch with straight back · heavy deadlifts / bent-over rows → glute bridge, bird dog, seated rows · jumping → step-based moves.
areas.cautions: AVOID traditional sit-ups and crunches and loaded toe-touches — McGill's research is clear that repetitive spinal flexion under load aggravates backs. Avoid twisting stretches early in a flare. Stop and see a clinician urgently for: numbness/weakness in the legs, bladder or bowel changes, or pain shooting below the knee. Also: avoid spinal flexion in the first hour after waking (discs are hydrated and stiffer — McGill's "spine hygiene" point).
redFlags: Numbness or weakness in the legs.
areas.laterCandidates: hip hinge practice (unloaded, teaches safe lifting), wall angels (thoracic mobility), foam-roller thoracic extension (needs a roller — optional), walking program (the single best "exercise" for backs).

areas.name: Shoulder
areas.intro: rotator-cuff tendinopathy / impingement from overhead work and pressing, plus rounded shoulders from driving. Rehab is strictly phased (MOON Shoulder Group protocol): mobility first, strengthening only once range of motion is nearly pain-free — strengthening too early is the classic mistake.

exercises.name: Pendulum swings
exercises.how: Lean forward, let the sore arm dangle, swing gently in small circles using body movement, 1–2 min. Uses gravity, not muscle — the safe first move.
steps: Lean forward, let the sore arm dangle, swing gently in small circles using body movement, 1–2 min.
Uses gravity, not muscle — the safe first move.

exercises.name: Cross-body stretch
exercises.how: Pull sore arm across chest with the other hand, hold 30 s. Stretches the posterior capsule.
steps: Pull sore arm across chest with the other hand, hold 30 s.
Stretches the posterior capsule.

exercises.name: Sleeper stretch
exercises.how: Lying on sore side, elbow at 90°, gently press forearm toward floor, hold 30 s.
steps: Lying on sore side, elbow at 90°, gently press forearm toward floor, hold 30 s.

exercises.name: Shoulder blade squeezes (scapular setting)
exercises.how: Sit/stand tall, gently squeeze shoulder blades together and slightly down, hold 5 s. Wakes up the stabilisers.
steps: Sit/stand tall, gently squeeze shoulder blades together and slightly down, hold 5 s.
Wakes up the stabilisers.

exercises.name: Isometric external rotation
exercises.how: Elbow at side, back of hand against a wall/doorframe, push outward without moving, hold 5–10 s. First strength step, no joint movement.
steps: Elbow at side, back of hand against a wall/doorframe, push outward without moving, hold 5–10 s.
First strength step, no joint movement.

exercises.name: Banded external rotation
exercises.how: Elbow tucked at side with a towel roll under the arm, rotate forearm outward against a light band, return slowly. Targets infraspinatus/teres minor.
steps: Elbow tucked at side with a towel roll under the arm, rotate forearm outward against a light band, return slowly.
Targets infraspinatus/teres minor.

exercises.name: Banded internal rotation
exercises.how: Mirror of #6, rotating forearm inward against the band. Targets subscapularis.
steps: Mirror of #6, rotating forearm inward against the band.
Targets subscapularis.

exercises.name: Side-lying external rotation
exercises.how: Lying on good side, sore arm on top with a light weight (0.5–1 kg — a water bottle works), rotate forearm to ceiling, lower over 3 s. EMG studies show this is the best isolated infraspinatus exercise.
steps: Lying on good side, sore arm on top with a light weight (0.5–1 kg — a water bottle works), rotate forearm to ceiling, lower over 3 s.
EMG studies show this is the best isolated infraspinatus exercise.

exercises.name: Scaption
exercises.how: Raise arm in the scapular plane (~30° in front of sideways), thumb up, light band/weight. The shoulder-friendly way to raise the arm.
steps: Raise arm in the scapular plane (~30° in front of sideways), thumb up, light band/weight.
The shoulder-friendly way to raise the arm.

exercises.name: Band pull-apart
exercises.how: Hold band at shoulder height, pull apart until it touches chest, squeeze shoulder blades. Rear delts + external rotators.
steps: Hold band at shoulder height, pull apart until it touches chest, squeeze shoulder blades.
Rear delts + external rotators.

exercises.name: Band face pull
exercises.how: Band anchored at eye level (truck door handle works), pull to bridge of nose, elbows flared, fists rotate out at the end.
steps: Band anchored at eye level (truck door handle works), pull to bridge of nose, elbows flared, fists rotate out at the end.

exercises.name: Wall angels
exercises.how: Back against wall, arms in goalpost shape, slowly slide up and down without arching the back. Mobility + posture.
steps: Back against wall, arms in goalpost shape, slowly slide up and down without arching the back.
Mobility + posture.

areas.swapsText: overhead press / push-ups → scaption, band pull-aparts · dips → wall push-ups · pull-ups → band rows · burpees → squat + step-back (no push-up) · planks → forearm plank on knees if the shoulder complains.

swaps.match: shoulder press|upside down|squat and press|squat & press|lateral raise|front raise|front lateral|side lateral
push.?ups?|pusups|pushup|dive bomber|bench dip|tricep bench|chest press|band press|band fly|chest fly

areas.cautions: do NOT start strengthening until range of motion is nearly pain-free — the MOON protocol milestone is active elevation above ~120° and pain at rest below 2/10. Avoid overhead pressing and behind-the-neck moves while painful. Sleeper stretch: gentle only, stop on sharp pain. Frozen shoulder (stiff in all directions, worse at night) needs a different, mobility-first approach — the app should flag "see a clinician" rather than push strengthening. Post-surgery shoulders follow the surgeon's protocol, not the app. If no improvement after 6–8 weeks of consistent work, get assessed.
redFlags: After shoulder surgery, follow the surgeon's protocol, not the app.
Stiff in every direction and worse at night (possible frozen shoulder): see a clinician instead of strengthening.
No improvement after 6–8 weeks of consistent work.
areas.laterCandidates: wall push-up plus (serratus), prone T's and Y's (lying face down, arms out), doorway chest stretch, cane-assisted range of motion, shoulder rolls.

swapMoves.name: Step jacks
swapMoves.how: Step one foot out to the side while the arms rise, step back in. No jumping.

swapMoves.name: Incline push-up + step-back (no jump)
swapMoves.how: Hands on the truck step or a counter, do one incline push-up, then step the feet back in one at a time and stand up. No jump.

swapMoves.name: Squat + step-back (no push-up)
swapMoves.how: Squat down, hands to the floor or a step, step the feet back to a plank and back in, stand up. No push-up, no jump.

swapMoves.name: Marching in place
swapMoves.how: Stand tall and march, lifting the knees to a comfortable height, arms swinging.

swapMoves.name: Forearm plank on knees
swapMoves.how: Forearms on the floor, knees down, body straight from head to knees. Hold.

swapMoves.name: Wall push-ups
swapMoves.how: Hands on a wall (or the truck) at shoulder height, step back, bend the elbows to bring the chest toward the wall, push back.

swapMoves.name: Supported step-ups
swapMoves.how: Low step, one hand on a rail or the truck for balance, step up and down slowly, leading with the sore leg.

swapMoves.name: Seated band row
swapMoves.how: Sit with legs out, band around the feet, pull the handles to the ribs, squeeze the shoulder blades, return slowly. Keep the pull light and pain-free.

dynamic.how: Big slow circles, 10 each direction, forward and back.
steps: Big slow circles, 10 each direction, forward and back.

dynamic.how: Hold the truck/wall, swing one leg forward–back 10×, then side-to-side 10× each leg.
steps: Hold the truck/wall, swing one leg forward–back 10×, then side-to-side 10× each leg.

dynamic.how: On all fours, 8–10 slow rounds arching and rounding the spine.
steps: On all fours, 8–10 slow rounds arching and rounding the spine.

steps: Step into a deep lunge, elbow to floor inside the front foot, then rotate open; 4–5 per side.

steps: 10 slow rolls each way; hands on hips, 10 circles each direction.

steps: Arms overhead, lean to one side, hold, switch.

steps: Kneeling lunge, push hips forward, hold.

steps: Seated, ankle on opposite knee, lean forward gently.

routines.name: Marine Corps — Daily 16
routines.space: A parking space; jog in place
routines.intro: The USMC's official warm-up/conditioning program. Versions vary slightly between units; the sequence below is the Daily 16 as taught at the Staff NCO / Career courses at Quantico. Sources: full official text at https://archive.org/stream/US_Marine_Corps_Daily_16_Program/US_Marine_Corps_Daily_16_Program_djvu.txt ; Quantico sequence at https://www.oo-rah.com/semper-fitness/platoon-pt-daily-16 ; also summarised at https://trainerjosh.com/workouts/marine-corps-workout/.

items.name: Slow jog
items.how: Easy jog around the field — in the truck world: march/jog in place beside the truck, 1–2 min. Raises temperature and heart rate.

items.name: Slow joint rotations
items.how: Neck, arm circles, hips, knees, ankles — 10 counts each direction. Loosens every joint before anything else.

items.name: Reach for the sky
items.how: Hands overhead, stretch as tall as possible.

items.name: Chest stretch
items.how: Hands clasped behind back, lift gently (or use a door frame).

items.name: Upper back stretch
items.how: Arms forward, round the upper back.

items.name: Tricep stretch
items.how: One arm overhead, pull the elbow gently with the other hand.

items.name: Hip and back stretch
items.how: Standing, hands on knees, gentle round-and-arch of the back and hips.

items.name: Groin stretch
items.how: Wide stance, shift weight side to side.

items.name: Thigh stretch
items.how: Standing quad stretch, hold the truck for balance.

items.name: Hamstring stretch
items.how: Heel on a low step, hinge forward from the hips.

items.name: Calf stretch
items.how: Wall stretch, back heel down, knee straight then bent.

items.name: Stride jumps
items.how: Jumping jacks in place, 10 reps, 4-count. Truck swap: step jacks if knees/ankles are flagged in the Recovery tab.

flagged.name: Step jacks
flagged.how: Step one foot out to the side while the arms rise, step back in. No jumping.

items.name: Steam engines
items.how: Standing, march opposite elbow to opposite knee, 10 reps.

items.name: Cross-country skier
items.how: Alternating arm/leg swing in a striding motion, 10 reps.

items.name: Bicycle crunches
items.how: Lying, pedal the legs, elbow to opposite knee, 10 reps.

items.name: Cool-down stretches
items.how: Repeat stretches 4–11 to close.

routines.name: Army — PRT Preparation Drill
routines.space: A mat or floor patch for 3 floor moves
routines.intro: The Army's official warm-up: 10 exercises in a fixed order, 5–10 reps each at a slow tempo, done before every training session. Sources: ATP 7-22.02 (Oct 2020), full text at https://fliphtml5.com/xgwlo/pgnq ; summaries at https://www.gymnasetips.com/army-prt/ and https://www.bespokepost.com/field-guide/army-approved-stretches-for-any-workout ; demo video of all 10 drills: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdnNxc4xh6O/.

items.name: Bend and Reach
items.how: Squat down and reach to the floor, stand and reach overhead. Controlled, no bouncing. 5–10 reps.

items.name: Rear Lunge
items.how: Step back into a deep lunge, arms overhead, return. Alternate legs.

items.name: High Jumper
items.how: Small jump, legs spread, arms overhead, land soft and repeat. Truck swap: step-out version with no jump if knees/ankles are flagged.

flagged.name: High Jumper (no jump)
flagged.how: Step out to the side with arms overhead instead of jumping, step back in.

items.name: Rower
items.how: Lying on back, sit up rowing the arms as knees come to chest, then extend back out. Core + hip flexors.

items.name: Squat Bender
items.how: Squat, then fold forward touching the floor, return to standing.

items.name: Windmill
items.how: Wide stance, rotate the torso and touch opposite toes, alternating sides. Rotate from the hips, knees slightly bent.

items.name: Forward Lunge
items.how: Step forward into a lunge, drive back to standing. Alternate legs.

items.name: Prone Row
items.how: Lying face down, lift chest and arms, squeeze the shoulder blades together.

items.name: Bent-Leg Body Twist
items.how: Lying on back, knees bent, drop knees side to side while shoulders stay on the floor.

items.name: Push-Up
items.how: 5–10 standard push-ups (from knees if needed).

routines.cautions: needs a mat or floor patch beside the truck for #4, #8, #9; everything else is standing. Doctrine timing is ~5–8 min at a brisk clip; at a careful slow tempo (which is how it should be done) it's 10–15 min.

routines.name: Ba Duan Jin — Eight Pieces of Brocade (Qigong)
routines.intro: Eight movements, same order every time, 4–8 slow reps each, 10–15 min total, standing, no equipment, about one mat of space. Standardised by China's Health Qigong Management Center (2003); written record back to the Song dynasty (~900 years). Sources: https://wudang.academy/en/page/qigong-baduanjin ; https://www.wikiqigong.com/articles/baduanjin/ ; https://globalspiritualstudies.com/eight-brocades/.

items.name: Two Hands Hold Up the Heavens
items.how: Interlace fingers, float palms up the centre line and press gently to the sky, then lower. Full-body stretch, opens the breath.

items.name: Drawing the Bow to Shoot the Hawk
items.how: Wide easy stance, one hand points out to the side while the other draws back across the chest like a bowstring; alternate. Opens chest and shoulders.

items.name: Separating Heaven and Earth
items.how: One palm presses up above the head while the other presses down beside the hip; alternate. Stretches the waist and sides.

items.name: Looking Back (Wise Owl Gazes Backward)
items.how: Arms relaxed, slowly turn the head to look behind; alternate. Releases neck and shoulders.

items.name: Swaying the Head and Shaking the Tail
items.how: Low stance, slow lean and sway side to side. Mobilises the spine and hips.

items.name: Two Hands Hold the Feet
items.how: Fold forward, hands reaching toward the feet, lengthening the spine and the backs of the legs.

items.name: Clenching the Fists and Gazing Fiercely
items.how: Slow controlled punch from a low stance, alternate arms, focused gaze. Builds a little heat and strength.

items.name: Lifting the Heels (Bouncing on the Toes)
items.how: Rise onto the balls of the feet and drop the heels gently, 7×, then shake the whole body loose to finish.

routines.cautions: #1 — with shoulder problems, lift only as high as comfortable; #3 — don't arch the low back; #5–#7 — keep the stance high and knees tracking over the toes.

routines.name: Tai Chi "Daily Dozen" joint loosening
routines.bestFor: When something specific is stiff; most truck-friendly
routines.intro: Twelve joint rotations, head to toe, 10 rotations each direction per joint, ~10 min. The standard Chen-style warm-up. Sources: https://dochenstyletaichi.com/tai-chi-warm-ups-part-1-upper-body/ (full list + demo video linked at the bottom of the page) ; https://wanghaijuntaichi.com/warm-up-joint-loosening-exercises/ (Grandmaster Wang Haijun's 18-exercise version).

items.name: Neck rotation
items.how: Slow head circles, 10 each way; move only the neck, keep shoulders still.

items.name: Shoulder rotation
items.how: Big slow shoulder circles, both directions.

items.name: Elbow rotation 1
items.how: Arms out at 45°, silk-reel the hands in circles (spiral the forearms).

items.name: Elbow rotation 2
items.how: Hands circle to the hips and back out, silk-reeling throughout.

items.name: Wrist rotation 1
items.how: Wrist circles one way, 10 reps.

items.name: Wrist rotation 2
items.how: Wrist circles the other way, 10 reps.

items.name: Finger rotation
items.how: Spread the fingers wide and circle them.

items.name: Waist rotation
items.how: Hands on hips, circle the waist both directions.

items.name: Hip rotation
items.how: Hands on hips, smooth hip circles both directions, 2 min minimum — the single most valuable move for low-back pain in this whole list (per the Chen-style back-pain guide).

items.name: Knee rotation
items.how: Feet together, knees slightly bent, small circles both ways.

items.name: Ankle rotation
items.how: One foot at a time, circles both ways.

items.name: Three leg stretches
items.how: Front, side, and cross leg stretches to finish.

routines.cautions: Wang Haijun's version adds: slap the body lightly, shake the fingers down and to the side, and stretch the hips/groin and hamstrings while holding the feet — all usable as optional extras.
